info.title: Kalligator API
info.description:
The Kalligator API gives you all the hacker functions of the website. Use it to find programs, write and submit reports, upload evidence, and reply to the triage agent.

Send `Authorization: Bearer kal_...` with an API key from the **API keys** section of your account page. The full guide is at https://docs.kalligator.com/api-reference/introduction.

GET /api/programs.description:
Returns published programs, newest update first. Each filter takes comma-separated values. The API ignores unknown values.

The `Authorization` header is optional. Send it to include the private programs that invite your verified email. An invalid or empty header gives `401`.

`counts[filter][option]` tells you how many programs that option shows, given the other filters.

limit.description: Programs on each page, from 1 to 50.

page.description: Page number, from 1. A page after the end gives the last page.

GET /api/programs/{program_id}.description:
Returns one program with its policy text in Markdown: description, scope, exclusions, rules, eligibility, and disclosure terms. Read all of these before you test.

An unpublished program gives `404`. A private program gives `404` unless your token belongs to an invited hacker.

GET /api/reports.description:
Returns your reports, newest update first.

To get the next page, send `next_cursor` as `cursor`. `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page.

To poll for changes, send the newest `updated_at` that you saw as `updated_since`. Use the `Z` form that the API returns. Read every page, then keep the newest `updated_at` of the first page for the next poll. `updated_at` changes on each status change, each draft save, and each file upload.

limit.description: Reports on each page, from 1 to 100.

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` value from the previous page.

updated_since.description: Return only reports changed after this time. Include a time zone, for example `2026-10-01T12:00:00Z`.

GET /api/reports/{report_id}.description: Returns one of your reports. A report that is not yours gives `404`.

PUT /api/reports/{report_id}.description:
Creates a draft or saves changes to a draft. You choose the report ID: make a new UUIDv4. Because the ID is yours, a retry never makes a duplicate report.

Send `revision: 0` for a new draft. After that, send the `revision` from the last response. If the draft changed in a different session, the API returns `409 revision_conflict` with the stored report in `current`.

You can only edit a report in `draft` status. You cannot change `program_id` after you create the draft. Your email must be verified.

report_id.description: A UUIDv4 that you make for a new draft, or the ID of your draft.

POST /api/reports/{report_id}/submit.description:
Submits a draft and starts triage. The report moves to `triaging`. Kalligator freezes the report content, its ready files, and the program policy at this time.

Submission needs all of these:

- A verified email.
- A Stripe payout account with status `ready`.
- A title, an asset, and a description with text below the template headings.
- No unfinished file uploads.
- A program with open intake and a reward pool that is not paused.
- Fewer than five active reports.

To submit again with the same `revision` is safe. The API returns the submitted report and does not start a second triage.

POST /api/reports/{report_id}/withdraw.description:
Withdraws a submitted report before the final decision. A queued triage turn stops. If the report holds an active-report slot (`triaging`, `needs_info`, or `paused`), it gives the slot back.

You cannot withdraw after a final decision (`409 invalid_state`). To withdraw a withdrawn report again is safe and makes no change.

PUT /api/reports/{report_id}/files/{file.description:
Uploads the raw bytes of one evidence file. Send the file MIME type as `Content-Type`, or `application/octet-stream`. The response is the updated report: use its new `revision` for your next change. A new upload adds 2 to the revision: one for the reservation and one when the file is ready. Always use the `revision` in the response. Do not add 1 yourself.

On a draft, the file attaches to the report. Before a final decision, the file waits as message evidence until you send it with a message.

Limits: 10 files on a draft, 10 MiB for each file, 10 pending message files, and 40 files on a report in total. To upload the same bytes with the same file ID again is safe.

file_id.description: A UUIDv4 that you make for this file.

name.description: The file name, for example `request.txt`. No folder separators or control characters.

GET /api/reports/{report_id}/files/{file.description: Downloads one ready file from your report as `application/octet-stream`.

DELETE /api/reports/{report_id}/files/{f.description: Removes a file from a draft, or a pending message file that you did not send. First remove all Markdown references to the file (`409 file_referenced`). Submitted files and sent files do not change.

GET /api/reports/{report_id}/messages.description: Returns the report thread, oldest first. `author` is `agent` for the triage agent, `researcher` for you, and `founder` for the Kalligator team.

POST /api/reports/{report_id}/messages.description:
Sends a message on the report thread before the final decision. Send a `body`, at least one file ID in `files`, or both.

If the report status is `needs_info`, your message is a reply. The report moves to `triaging` and the triage agent starts a new turn. In other statuses, the message does not change the status. The agent reads it on its next turn.

Each file must be a message file that you uploaded and that is `ready`. Your email must be verified.

GET /api/me.description: Returns your email, verification state, active-report count, and the last stored Stripe status. This call does not contact Stripe. For a fresh Stripe check, use `GET /api/stripe/status`.

GET /api/stripe/status.description: Gets a fresh status of your Stripe payout account. Submission needs `ready: true`. If Stripe has a problem, the status is `unavailable` with HTTP `200`. Your email must be verified.

POST /api/stripe/onboarding.description:
Returns a single-use Stripe onboarding link. Open it in a browser to set up or update your payout account.

This route needs a website sign-in. An API key gives `403 session_required`, so a leaked key cannot change where your rewards go. Use the **Payouts** section of your account page.

POST /api/auth/verification-email.description:
Sends an email with a verification link to the account email. If the email is already verified, the API sends nothing and returns `already_verified: true`.

Limits: one email each minute and five each hour.

POST /api/auth/password-reset.description:
Sends a password reset link if an account has this email. The response is the same when no account exists.

Limits: five requests each minute and 30 each hour from one address. One email each minute and five each hour to one email address.

GET /api/keys.description: Returns your API keys, newest first. The secret key does not show again after creation. This route needs a website sign-in.

POST /api/keys.description:
Creates an API key. The response is the only time that you see the secret `key`. Store it in a secret manager.

A `write` key can use all hacker routes. A `read` key can only use `GET`. Expiry is from 1 to 365 days (default 90), or `null` for no expiry. The limit is 100 keys. This route needs a website sign-in.

DELETE /api/keys/{key_id}.description: Deletes an API key. The key stops working immediately. This route needs a website sign-in.

key_id.description: The key `id` from the key list.

properties.demo: `true` for a demonstration program with test data.
properties.rewards: Reward in US dollars for each severity: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.
properties.policy_version: The version of the program policy and reward table. A report keeps the version that it was submitted under.
properties.private: `true` if only invited hackers can see the program.
properties.pool_paused: `true` if new submissions are paused because the reward pool is below the largest reward.

properties.rewards: Reward in US dollars for each severity: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.
properties.policy_version: The version of the program policy and reward table.
properties.private: `true` if only invited hackers can see the program.
properties.pool_paused: `true` if new submissions are paused because the reward pool is below the largest reward.
properties.scope: Markdown. The assets and hosts that you are permitted to test.
properties.exclusions: Markdown. Assets and flaw types that are out of scope.
properties.rules: Markdown. Rules of engagement for testing.
properties.eligibility: Markdown. Who can receive a reward.
properties.disclosure: Markdown. When and how you can publish details.

properties.program_id: The program for the report. You cannot change it after you create the draft.
properties.title: A short title, at most 180 characters.
properties.asset: The affected asset, for example a URL, host, app, or repository. At most 1000 characters.
properties.description: Markdown, at most 30000 characters. Use the headings for steps to reproduce, expected behavior, actual behavior, and security impact.
properties.cvss_vector: Optional. Your CVSS 3.1 base vector, for example `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`. Send an empty string for none.
properties.revision: `0` for a new draft. Otherwise the current `revision` of the report.

properties.status: The report status. See the report lifecycle guide.
properties.display_status: The status text that the website shows.
properties.revision: Increases when you save the draft, upload or remove a file, submit, or withdraw. Send the latest value with your next change.
properties.attachments: Files on the report, by file ID.
properties.submission: The frozen copy of the report, files, and program policy at submission. `null` for a draft.
properties.decision: The final decision and an optional message. `null` until a decision.
properties.payout: Your reward payment. `null` until the Kalligator team approves the reward.

properties.status: The report status. See the report lifecycle guide.
properties.display_status: The status text that the website shows.

properties.state: `ready` files can be referenced and downloaded. `uploading` and `failed` files block submission.
properties.sha256: The SHA-256 hash of the file bytes.
properties.message_id: The message that sent the file. `null` while the file waits.

properties.files: Up to 10 IDs of ready message files.

properties.name: A label for the key, 1 to 80 characters. For example, the name of your agent.
properties.scope: `write` (default) or `read`. A `read` key can only use `GET`.
properties.expires_in_days: Days until the key expires, from 1 to 365. Default 90. Send `null` for no expiry.

properties.key: The secret key. It starts with `kal_`. This is the only time that the API shows it.

properties.id: The key ID. Use it to delete the key. It is not the secret.
properties.hint: The first eight characters of the key.
properties.last_used_at: The last use. Updates at most once each minute.

properties.active_reports: Reports that hold a slot: `triaging`, `needs_info`, or `paused`.
properties.active_limit: The maximum number of active reports.

properties.status: The payout account status. Only `ready` permits submission.
properties.ready: `true` only when the server check passes.
properties.detail: A short sentence that tells you the next step.

properties.status: `approving`, then `transferred`, then `received`. `payout_failed` if the bank payout failed.

Error.description: Every error has this body. Make decisions on `code`, not on `detail`.

properties.current: Only on `409 revision_conflict`: the stored report.
